where εi∼Bernoulli⁡(1/2)\varepsilon_{i}\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(1/2), (ε1,…,εℓ)(\varepsilon_{1},\ldots,\varepsilon_{\ell}) are mutually independent and are independent of (G1,…,Gℓ)(G_{1},\ldots,G_{\ell}). Then (T1,…,Tℓ)(T_{1},\ldots,T_{\ell}) are independent, 𝔼⁡[Ti]=0\mathbb{E}[T_{i}]=0 and Ti2=Gi∼γ⁡(δi,δi−1)T_{i}^{2}=G_{i}\sim\gamma(\delta_{i},\delta_{i}^{-1}), so that Var⁡(Ti)=δi​δi−1=1\mathrm{Var}(T_{i})=\delta_{i}\delta_{i}^{-1}=1. Next, define 𝐃\mathbf{D} to be the diagonal matrix such that 𝐃i​i=λi1/2\mathbf{D}_{ii}=\lambda_{i}^{1/2} and define R1≔𝐃​TR_{1}\coloneqq\mathbf{D}T. Then 𝔼⁡[R1]=0\mathbb{E}[R_{1}]=0, and because Var⁡(Ti)=1\mathrm{Var}(T_{i})=1, we have 𝚺≔Cov⁡(R1)=𝐃2\mathbf{\Sigma}\coloneqq\mathrm{Cov}(R_{1})=\mathbf{D}^{2}, and

∥𝚺−1/2R1∥2\displaystyle\|\mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1/2}R_{1}\|^{2} =R1⊤​𝚺−1​R1=‖T‖2=∑i=1ℓTi2,\displaystyle=R_{1}^{\top}\mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1}R_{1}=\|T\|^{2}=\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}T_{i}^{2}, (216)
det(𝚺)−1/ℓ∥R1∥2\displaystyle\det(\mathbf{\Sigma})^{-1/\ell}\|R_{1}\|^{2} =det(𝚺)−1/ℓT⊤𝐃2T=∑i=1ℓδiTi2.\displaystyle=\det(\mathbf{\Sigma})^{-1/\ell}T^{\top}\mathbf{D}^{2}T=\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\delta_{i}T_{i}^{2}. (217)

We now apply Theorem 1.2 from [37], in order to describe the tail behaviour of both random variables above. For this, observe that δi​Ti2∼γ⁡(δi,1)\delta_{i}T_{i}^{2}\sim\gamma(\delta_{i},1). The Laplace transforms of ∑i=1ℓTi2\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}T_{i}^{2} and ∑i=1ℓδi​Ti2\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\delta_{i}T_{i}^{2} are then given by

ℒ1​(ω)\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{1}(\omega) ≔ℒ⁡(∑i=1ℓTi2)​(ω)=∏i=1ℓ1(1+δi−1​ω)δi,\displaystyle\coloneqq\mathcal{L}\bigg(\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}T_{i}^{2}\bigg)(\omega)=\prod_{i=1}^{\ell}\frac{1}{(1+\delta_{i}^{-1}\omega)^{\delta_{i}}}, (218)
ℒ2​(ω)\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{2}(\omega) ≔ℒ⁡(∑i=1ℓδi​Ti2)​(ω)=∏i=1ℓ1(1+ω)δi.\displaystyle\coloneqq\mathcal{L}\bigg(\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\delta_{i}T_{i}^{2}\bigg)(\omega)=\prod_{i=1}^{\ell}\frac{1}{(1+\omega)^{\delta_{i}}}. (219)

To apply Theorem 1.2 from [37], we need to identify the abscissa of convergence of ℒ1\mathcal{L}_{1} and ℒ2\mathcal{L}_{2}. The abscissa of convergence of a (probability) measure ν\nu over [0,∞)[0,\infty) is the unique scalar σ0∈ℝ∪{−∞}\sigma_{0}\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\} such that the integral f(z)=∫[0,+∞)e−z​tν(dt)f(z)=\int_{[0,+\infty)}e^{-zt}\nu(dt) converges for Re⁡(z)>σ0\mathrm{Re}(z)>\sigma_{0}, diverges for Re⁡(z)<σ0\mathrm{Re}(z)<\sigma_{0} and has a singularity at σ0\sigma_{0} [37], p 267. For ℒ1\mathcal{L}_{1} and ℒ2\mathcal{L}_{2}, it is clear from equations (218) and (219) that their abscissa of convergence are given by σ1≔−mini⁡δi<0\sigma_{1}\coloneqq-\min_{i}\delta_{i}<0 and σ2≔−1\sigma_{2}\coloneqq-1 respectively. We now apply [37], Theorem 1.2, on ℒ1\mathcal{L}_{1} and ℒ2\mathcal{L}_{2} (we check the conditions for applying this result at the end of the proof). This yields

limt→+∞logℙ(∥𝚺−1/2R1∥2>t)logℙ(det(𝚺)−1/ℓ∥R1∥2>t)=σ1σ2=−mini⁡δi−1=mini⁡δi<1.\displaystyle\lim_{t\rightarrow+\infty}\frac{\log\mathbb{P}(\|\mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1/2}R_{1}\|^{2}>t)}{\log\mathbb{P}(\det(\mathbf{\Sigma})^{-1/\ell}\|R_{1}\|^{2}>t)}=\frac{\sigma_{1}}{\sigma_{2}}=\frac{-\min_{i}\delta_{i}}{-1}=\min_{i}\delta_{i}<1. (220)

Indeed, if mini⁡δi≥1\min_{i}\delta_{i}\geq 1, then we would have λ1=…=λℓ\lambda_{1}=\ldots=\lambda_{\ell} which contradicts our assumption. Because both logarithms above are negative, this yields

logℙ(∥𝚺−1/2R1∥2>t)>logℙ(det(𝚺)−1/ℓ∥R1∥2>t)for large t.\displaystyle\log\mathbb{P}(\|\mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1/2}R_{1}\|^{2}>t)>\log\mathbb{P}(\det(\mathbf{\Sigma})^{-1/\ell}\|R_{1}\|^{2}>t)\ \ \ \text{for large $t$}. (221)

We then take the exponential of the equation above, we compare the resulting CDFs (this reverses the ordering w.r.t. “>>”) and we compare the inverses of those CDFs (this reverses back the ordering). We finally obtain that for α\alpha small enough,

q1−α(∥𝚺−1/2R1∥2)>q1−α(det(𝚺)−1/ℓ∥R1∥2).\displaystyle q_{1-\alpha}(\|\mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1/2}R_{1}\|^{2})>q_{1-\alpha}(\det(\mathbf{\Sigma})^{-1/\ell}\|R_{1}\|^{2}). (222)

In particular, for α\alpha small enough, Vol⁡(ℰα∞)>Vol⁡(ℬα∞)\mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{E}_{\alpha}^{\infty})>\mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_{\alpha}^{\infty}), which is the announced result. We now check the two technical conditions of [37], Theorem 1.2, on ℒ2\mathcal{L}_{2} (the proof is similar for ℒ1\mathcal{L}_{1}). First, for λ>0\lambda>0,

λ​log⁡ℒ2​(σ2+λ)\displaystyle\lambda\log\mathcal{L}_{2}(\sigma_{2}+\lambda) =−(∑i=1ℓδi)​λ​log⁡λ→λ→0+0.\displaystyle=-\bigg(\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\delta_{i}\bigg)\lambda\log\lambda\xrightarrow[\lambda\rightarrow 0^{+}]{}0. (223)

Second, for all 0<λ1≤λ20<\lambda_{1}\leq\lambda_{2} sufficiently small,

ℒ2​(σ2+λ2)ℒ2​(σ2+λ1)\displaystyle\frac{\mathcal{L}_{2}(\sigma_{2}+\lambda_{2})}{\mathcal{L}_{2}(\sigma_{2}+\lambda_{1})} =∏i=1ℓ(λ1λ2)−δi=(λ2λ1)−γ,\displaystyle=\prod_{i=1}^{\ell}\bigg(\frac{\lambda_{1}}{\lambda_{2}}\bigg)^{-\delta_{i}}=\bigg(\frac{\lambda_{2}}{\lambda_{1}}\bigg)^{-\gamma}, (224)

with γ≔∑i=1ℓδi>0\gamma\coloneqq\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\delta_{i}>0. From [37], equation (1.3) and Lemma 3.1, this finishes the proof. ∎

Proof of Lemma B.6.

In this proof, we denote m≔𝔼⁡[V1]m\coloneqq\mathbb{E}[V_{1}], m^n≔n−1​∑i=1nVi\widehat{m}_{n}\coloneqq n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}V_{i} for notational conciseness. We also denote

Ti\displaystyle T_{i} =𝚺λ−1/2(Vi−m),T^i=𝚺^n,λ−1/2(Vi−m^n),νn=1n∑j=1nδTj,ν^n=1n∑j=1nδT^j.\displaystyle=\mathbf{\Sigma}_{\lambda}^{-1/2}(V_{i}-m),\ \ \ \widehat{T}_{i}=\widehat{\mathbf{\Sigma}}_{n,\lambda}^{-1/2}(V_{i}-\widehat{m}_{n}),\ \ \ \nu_{n}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\delta_{T_{j}},\ \ \ \widehat{\nu}_{n}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\delta_{\widehat{T}_{j}}. (225)

Note that we are interested in the quantiles of (‖T^1‖2,…,‖T^n‖2)(\|\widehat{T}_{1}\|^{2},\ldots,\|\widehat{T}_{n}\|^{2}), since qn,α=n​p(nα)q_{n,\alpha}=np_{(n_{\alpha})} and n​pi,n=‖T^i‖2np_{i,n}=\|\widehat{T}_{i}\|^{2}. Below we borrow the empirical process notation, νn​(f)=n−1​∑j=1nf⁡(Tj)\nu_{n}(f)=n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{n}f(T_{j}). The proof is carried out by studying the empirical characteristic function. Let t∈ℝpt\in\mathbb{R}^{p}. From the SLLN,

νn​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)=1n​∑j=1nei​⟨t,Tj⟩→a.s.𝔼⁡[ei​⟨t,T1⟩].\displaystyle\nu_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}e^{i\langle t,T_{j}\rangle}\xrightarrow{a.s.}\mathbb{E}\big[e^{i\langle t,T_{1}\rangle}\big]. (226)

Thus, for all t∈ℝt\in\mathbb{R}, νn​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)→𝔼⁡[ei​⟨t,T1⟩]\nu_{n}(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle})\rightarrow\mathbb{E}\big[e^{i\langle t,T_{1}\rangle}\big] a.s.. We then prove below that thanks to the continuity of the characteristic functions and the separability of ℝp\mathbb{R}^{p}, we can interchange the “a.s.” and “∀t∈ℝp\forall t\in\mathbb{R}^{p}” to obtain that almost surely,

∀t∈ℝp,νn​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)→n→∞𝔼⁡[ei​⟨t,T1⟩].\displaystyle\forall t\in\mathbb{R}^{p},\ \ \ \nu_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)\xrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{}\mathbb{E}\big[e^{i\langle t,T_{1}\rangle}\big]. (227)

Let us prove this fact. Set 𝒟=ℚp\mathcal{D}=\mathbb{Q}^{p}, which is a countable dense subset of ℝp\mathbb{R}^{p}. From equation (226), for all t∈𝒟t\in\mathcal{D}, there exists Ωt\Omega_{t} with ℙ⁡(Ωt)=1\mathbb{P}(\Omega_{t})=1 such that for all ω∈Ωt,νn​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)→a.s.𝔼⁡[ei​⟨t,T1⟩]\omega\in\Omega_{t},\ \ \nu_{n}(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle})\xrightarrow{a.s.}\mathbb{E}\big[e^{i\langle t,T_{1}\rangle}\big]. We set Ω′≔∩t∈𝒟Ωt\Omega^{\prime}\coloneqq\cap_{t\in\mathcal{D}}\Omega_{t}, which has probability one and aim at proving that for all ω∈Ω′\omega\in\Omega^{\prime}, equation (227) holds. Let ω∈Ω′\omega\in\Omega^{\prime}, t∈ℝpt\in\mathbb{R}^{p}, ε>0\varepsilon>0 and t′∈𝒟t^{\prime}\in\mathcal{D} to be chosen later. We can write

|νn​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)−𝔼⁡[ei​⟨t,T1⟩]|\displaystyle\Big|\nu_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)-\mathbb{E}\big[e^{i\langle t,T_{1}\rangle}\big]\Big| ≤|νn​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)−νn​(ei​⟨t′,⋅⟩)|+|νn​(ei​⟨t′,⋅⟩)−𝔼⁡[ei⁡⟨t′,T1⟩]|+|𝔼⁡[ei⁡⟨t′,T1⟩]−𝔼⁡[ei​⟨t,T1⟩]|.\displaystyle\leq\Big|\nu_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)-\nu_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t^{\prime},\cdot\rangle}\Big)\Big|+\Big|\nu_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t^{\prime},\cdot\rangle}\Big)-\mathbb{E}\big[e^{i\langle t^{\prime},T_{1}\rangle}\big]\Big|+\big|\mathbb{E}\big[e^{i\langle t^{\prime},T_{1}\rangle}\big]-\mathbb{E}\big[e^{i\langle t,T_{1}\rangle}\big]\big|.

In the last term above, t′t^{\prime} can be chosen such that this term is smaller than ε/3\varepsilon/3 from the continuity of t↦𝔼⁡[ei​⟨t,T1⟩]t\mapsto\mathbb{E}\big[e^{i\langle t,T_{1}\rangle}\big] and the density of 𝒟\mathcal{D}, and the second term is smaller than ε/3\varepsilon/3 for all nn large enough, since equation (226) applies for t′∈𝒟t^{\prime}\in\mathcal{D}. Finally, for the first term,

|νn​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)−νn​(ei​⟨t′,⋅⟩)|\displaystyle\Big|\nu_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)-\nu_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t^{\prime},\cdot\rangle}\Big)\Big| ≤1n​∑j=1n|ei​⟨t,Tj⟩−ei⁡⟨t′,Tj⟩|=2n​∑j=1n|sin⁡(⟨t−t′,Tj⟩2)|≤(1n​∑j=1n‖Tj‖)​‖t−t′‖.\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\Big|e^{i\langle t,T_{j}\rangle}-e^{i\langle t^{\prime},{T}_{j}\rangle}\Big|=\frac{2}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\bigg|\sin\bigg(\frac{\langle t-t^{\prime},{T}_{j}\rangle}{2}\bigg)\bigg|\leq\bigg(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\|T_{j}\|\bigg)\|t-t^{\prime}\|. (228)

From the SLLN, the sum above is bounded by some Mω>0M_{\omega}>0 for nn large enough, and thus t′t^{\prime} can also be chosen (as a function of ω\omega) such that this term is smaller than ε/3\varepsilon/3. We have thus proved that almost surely, equation (227) holds.

We now prove that equation (227) also holds for ν^n\widehat{\nu}_{n}, and work similarly as above. For this, observe that for all t∈ℝpt\in\mathbb{R}^{p},

|ν^n​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)−νn​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)|\displaystyle\Big|\widehat{\nu}_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)-\nu_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)\Big| ≤1n​∑j=1n|ei​⟨t,T^j⟩−ei​⟨t,Tj⟩|=2n​∑j=1n|sin⁡(⟨t,T^j−Tj⟩2)|≤‖t‖n​∑j=1n‖T^j−Tj‖.\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\Big|e^{i\langle t,\widehat{T}_{j}\rangle}-e^{i\langle t,{T}_{j}\rangle}\Big|=\frac{2}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\bigg|\sin\bigg(\frac{\langle t,\widehat{T}_{j}-{T}_{j}\rangle}{2}\bigg)\bigg|\leq\frac{\|t\|}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\|\widehat{T}_{j}-{T}_{j}\|. (229)

Furthermore, using the matrix operator norm such that ‖M​x‖≤‖M‖Op​‖x‖\|Mx\|\leq\|M\|_{\mathrm{Op}}\|x\|,

‖T^j−Tj‖\displaystyle\|\widehat{T}_{j}-{T}_{j}\| =∥(𝚺λ−1/2−𝚺^n,λ−1/2)Vj−𝚺λ−1/2m+𝚺^n,λ−1/2m^n∥\displaystyle=\Big\|\Big(\mathbf{\Sigma}_{\lambda}^{-1/2}-\widehat{\mathbf{\Sigma}}_{n,\lambda}^{-1/2}\Big)V_{j}-\mathbf{\Sigma}_{\lambda}^{-1/2}m+\widehat{\mathbf{\Sigma}}_{n,\lambda}^{-1/2}\widehat{m}_{n}\Big\|
≤∥𝚺λ−1/2−𝚺^n,λ−1/2∥Op∥Vj∥+∥𝚺λ−1/2m−𝚺^n,λ−1/2m^n∥.\displaystyle\leq\Big\|\mathbf{\Sigma}_{\lambda}^{-1/2}-\widehat{\mathbf{\Sigma}}_{n,\lambda}^{-1/2}\Big\|_{\mathrm{Op}}\|V_{j}\|+\big\|\mathbf{\Sigma}_{\lambda}^{-1/2}m-\widehat{\mathbf{\Sigma}}_{n,\lambda}^{-1/2}\widehat{m}_{n}\Big\|.

From equation (167), the continuous mapping theorem and the SLLN, for all t≠0t\neq 0 (the case t=0t=0 is trivial),

1‖t‖​|ν^n​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)−νn​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)|\displaystyle\frac{1}{\|t\|}\Big|\widehat{\nu}_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)-\nu_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)\Big| ≤∥𝚺λ−1/2−𝚺^n,λ−1/2∥Op(1n∑j=1n∥Vj∥)+∥𝚺λ−1/2m−𝚺^n,λ−1/2m^n∥→n→∞a.s.0.\displaystyle\leq\Big\|\mathbf{\Sigma}_{\lambda}^{-1/2}-\widehat{\mathbf{\Sigma}}_{n,\lambda}^{-1/2}\Big\|_{\mathrm{Op}}\bigg(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\|V_{j}\|\bigg)+\big\|\mathbf{\Sigma}_{\lambda}^{-1/2}m-\widehat{\mathbf{\Sigma}}_{n,\lambda}^{-1/2}\widehat{m}_{n}\Big\|\ \ \xrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{a.s.}0. (230)

Note that for 𝚺^n,λ−1/2→𝚺λ−1/2\widehat{\mathbf{\Sigma}}_{n,\lambda}^{-1/2}\rightarrow\mathbf{\Sigma}_{\lambda}^{-1/2} to hold a.s., we either require that λ>0\lambda>0 or min⁡Spec​𝚺>0\min\mathrm{Spec}\mathbf{\Sigma}>0, so that we can apply the same arguments as those at the end of the proof of Proposition 4.1. Also, the a.s. convergence of equation (230) does not depend on tt, as the bound on the right-hand side of equation (230) does not depend on tt. Hence, almost surely,

∀t∈ℝp,|ν^n​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)−νn​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)|→n→∞0.\displaystyle\forall t\in\mathbb{R}^{p},\ \ \ \Big|\widehat{\nu}_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)-\nu_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)\Big|\xrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{}0. (231)

Combining equation (231) with equation (227), we finally obtain that almost surely,

∀t∈ℝp,ν^n​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)→n→∞𝔼⁡[ei​⟨t,T1⟩].\displaystyle\forall t\in\mathbb{R}^{p},\ \ \ \widehat{\nu}_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)\xrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{}\mathbb{E}\big[e^{i\langle t,T_{1}\rangle}\big]. (232)

Applying Lévy’s theorem sample by sample for ω∈Ω′\omega\in\Omega^{\prime}, we deduce that almost surely, in the Prokhorov metric for the weak convergence of measures over ℝp\mathbb{R}^{p},

ν^n→n→∞νT1.\displaystyle\widehat{\nu}_{n}\xlongrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{}\nu_{T_{1}}. (233)

Above, νT1\nu_{T_{1}} is the probability measure of T1T_{1}, defined over ℝp\mathbb{R}^{p}. Applying pushforward integration with the continuous map N⁡(x)=‖x‖2N(x)=\|x\|^{2}, almost surely (in the Prokhorov metric for probability measures over ℝ\mathbb{R}),

N#​ν^n=1n​∑j=1δ‖T^i‖2→n→∞N#​νT1≕ν‖T1‖2.\displaystyle N_{\#}\widehat{\nu}_{n}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}\delta_{\|\widehat{T}_{i}\|^{2}}\xlongrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{}N_{\#}\nu_{T_{1}}\eqqcolon\nu_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}}. (234)

Hence, almost surely, for all t∈ℝt\in\mathbb{R} which is a continuity point of F‖T1‖2F_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}}, where F‖T1‖2F_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}} denotes the CDF of ‖T1‖2\|T_{1}\|^{2},

F^n​(t)=1n​∑j=1n𝟙​(‖T^i‖2≤t)→n→∞F‖T1‖2​(t).\displaystyle\widehat{F}_{n}(t)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathbbm{1}({\|\widehat{T}_{i}\|^{2}\leq t})\xlongrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{}F_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}}(t). (235)

We now denote Q‖T1‖2Q_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}} the quantile function of ‖T1‖2\|T_{1}\|^{2} and Q^n\widehat{Q}_{n} the empirical quantile function of (‖T^1‖2,…,‖T^n‖2)(\|\widehat{T}_{1}\|^{2},\ldots,\|\widehat{T}_{n}\|^{2}). From equation (235) and [47], Lemma 21.2, we have that, almost surely, for all β∈(0,1)\beta\in(0,1) which is a continuity point of Q‖T1‖2Q_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}},

Q^n​(β)=F^n−1​(β)→n→∞Q‖T1‖2​(β).\displaystyle\widehat{Q}_{n}(\beta)=\widehat{F}_{n}^{-1}(\beta)\xlongrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{}Q_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}}(\beta). (236)

In particular, this holds for β=1−α\beta=1-\alpha, since we have assumed that 1−α1-\alpha was a continuity point of Q‖T1‖2Q_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}}. To finish, we need to show that equation (236) also holds for the order statistics qn,α=Q^n​(n+1n​(1−α))q_{n,\alpha}=\widehat{Q}_{n}(\frac{n+1}{n}(1-\alpha)). For this, from the assumptions, let 𝒱\mathcal{V} be a neighbourhood of 1−α1-\alpha such that Q‖T1‖2Q_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}} is continuous on 𝒱\mathcal{V}, and let M>0M>0 be such that 1−α+1/M∈𝒱1-\alpha+1/M\in\mathcal{V}. There exists nn large enough such that n+1n​(1−α)≤1−α+1/M\frac{n+1}{n}(1-\alpha)\leq 1-\alpha+1/M. Hence, from the monotony of the empirical quantile, we have that for all such nn,

Q^n​(1−α)≤Q^n​(n+1n​(1−α))≤Q^n​(1−α+1/M).\displaystyle\widehat{Q}_{n}(1-\alpha)\leq\widehat{Q}_{n}\bigg(\frac{n+1}{n}(1-\alpha)\bigg)\leq\widehat{Q}_{n}(1-\alpha+1/M). (237)

From equation (236) and the continuity of Q‖T1‖2Q_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}} at both 1−α1-\alpha and 1−α+1/M1-\alpha+1/M, almost surely,

Q‖T1‖2​(1−α)\displaystyle Q_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}}(1-\alpha) ≤lim infnQ^n​(n+1n​(1−α))≤lim supnQ^n​(n+1n​(1−α))≤Q‖T1‖2​(1−α+1/M).\displaystyle\leq\liminf_{n}\widehat{Q}_{n}\bigg(\frac{n+1}{n}(1-\alpha)\bigg)\leq\limsup_{n}\widehat{Q}_{n}\bigg(\frac{n+1}{n}(1-\alpha)\bigg)\leq Q_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}}(1-\alpha+1/M).

Since this equation holds for all M>0M>0 large enough, we have that lim infnQ^n​(n+1n​(1−α))=lim supnQ^n​(n+1n​(1−α))\liminf_{n}\widehat{Q}_{n}(\frac{n+1}{n}(1-\alpha))=\limsup_{n}\widehat{Q}_{n}(\frac{n+1}{n}(1-\alpha)), hence the sequence (Q^n​(n+1n​(1−α)))n(\widehat{Q}_{n}(\frac{n+1}{n}(1-\alpha)))_{n} is convergent and almost surely,

qn,α=Q^n​(n+1n​(1−α))→n→∞Q‖T1‖2​(1−α)=q1−αℰ.\displaystyle q_{n,\alpha}=\widehat{Q}_{n}\bigg(\frac{n+1}{n}(1-\alpha)\bigg)\xlongrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{}Q_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}}(1-\alpha)=q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathcal{E}}. (238)

This finishes the proof of equation (103). We now prove equation (104). For this, introduce mX=𝔼⁡[X1]m^{X}=\mathbb{E}[X_{1}], m^nX≔n−1​∑j=1nXi\widehat{m}_{n}^{X}\coloneqq n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{n}X_{i}, and

Ui\displaystyle U_{i} ≔(𝚺λ11)−1/2(Xi−mX),U^i≔(𝚺^n,λ11)−1/2(Xi−m^nX),\displaystyle\coloneqq(\mathbf{\Sigma}_{\lambda}^{11})^{-1/2}(X_{i}-m^{X}),\ \ \ \widehat{U}_{i}\coloneqq(\widehat{\mathbf{\Sigma}}_{n,\lambda}^{11})^{-1/2}(X_{i}-\widehat{m}_{n}^{X}), (239)
Ki\displaystyle K_{i} ≔(TiUi),K^i≔(T^iU^i),μn=1n​∑j=1nδKj,μ^n=1n​∑j=1nδK^j.\displaystyle\coloneqq\begin{pmatrix}T_{i}\\ U_{i}\end{pmatrix},\ \ \ \widehat{K}_{i}\coloneqq\begin{pmatrix}\widehat{T}_{i}\\ \widehat{U}_{i}\end{pmatrix},\ \ \ \mu_{n}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\delta_{K_{j}},\ \ \ \widehat{\mu}_{n}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\delta_{\widehat{K}_{j}}. (240)

We quickly show why we still have that almost surely,

∀t∈ℝp+k,μ^n​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)→n→∞𝔼⁡[ei​⟨t,K1⟩].\displaystyle\forall t\in\mathbb{R}^{p+k},\ \ \ \widehat{\mu}_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)\xlongrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{}\mathbb{E}\big[e^{i\langle t,K_{1}\rangle}\big]. (241)

First, equation (227) still holds when replacing TiT_{i} with KiK_{i} because the KiK_{i} remain iid, and the separability of ℝp+k\mathbb{R}^{p+k} and the continuity of t↦𝔼⁡[ei​⟨t,K1⟩]t\mapsto\mathbb{E}\big[e^{i\langle t,K_{1}\rangle}\big] still hold : that is,

∀t∈ℝp+k,μn​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)→n→∞𝔼⁡[ei​⟨t,K1⟩].\displaystyle\forall t\in\mathbb{R}^{p+k},\ \ \ \mu_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)\xlongrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{}\mathbb{E}\big[e^{i\langle t,K_{1}\rangle}\big]. (242)

We now show that equation (231) still holds when replacing TiT_{i} with KiK_{i} and T^i\widehat{T}_{i} with K^i\widehat{K}_{i}. We start from the bound

‖K^j−Kj‖=‖T^i−Ti‖2+‖U^i−Ui‖2≤‖T^i−Ti‖+‖U^i−Ui‖.\displaystyle\|\widehat{K}_{j}-K_{j}\|=\sqrt{\|\widehat{T}_{i}-T_{i}\|^{2}+\|\widehat{U}_{i}-U_{i}\|^{2}}\leq\|\widehat{T}_{i}-T_{i}\|+\|\widehat{U}_{i}-U_{i}\|. (243)

This bound implies that (see equation (229)) for all t∈ℝp+k,t≠0t\in\mathbb{R}^{p+k},t\neq 0,

1‖t‖​|μ^n​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)−μn​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)|≤1n​∑j=1n‖K^j−Kj‖≤1n​∑j=1n‖T^j−Tj‖+1n​∑j=1n‖U^j−Uj‖.\displaystyle\frac{1}{\|t\|}\Big|\widehat{\mu}_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)-\mu_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)\Big|\leq\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\|\widehat{K}_{j}-K_{j}\|\leq\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\|\widehat{T}_{j}-T_{j}\|+\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\|\widehat{U}_{j}-U_{j}\|. (244)

We can then use the same arguments on the two sums above as the ones that lead to equation (230), to obtain that a.s.,

∀t∈ℝp+k,|μ^n​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)−μn​(ei​⟨t,⋅⟩)|→n→∞0.\displaystyle\forall t\in\mathbb{R}^{p+k},\ \ \ \Big|\widehat{\mu}_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)-\mu_{n}\Big(e^{i\langle t,\cdot\rangle}\Big)\Big|\xrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{}0. (245)

Combining equations (242) and (245), we obtain equation (241). Equation (241) implies that in the Prokhorov metric, almost surely,

μ^n→n→∞μK\displaystyle\widehat{\mu}_{n}\xlongrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{}\mu_{K}

Using pushforward integration with the continuous map (x,y)↦‖x‖2−‖y‖2(x,y)\mapsto\|x\|^{2}-\|y\|^{2}, we obtain again that almost surely, for all t∈ℝt\in\mathbb{R} which is a continuity point of F‖T1‖2−‖U1‖2F_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}-\|U_{1}\|^{2}}, where F‖T1‖2−‖U1‖2F_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}-\|U_{1}\|^{2}} denotes the CDF of ‖T1‖2−‖U1‖2\|T_{1}\|^{2}-\|U_{1}\|^{2},

F^n​(t)=1n​∑j=1n𝟙​(‖T^i‖2−‖U^i‖2≤t)→n→∞F‖T1‖2−‖U1‖2​(t).\displaystyle\widehat{F}_{n}(t)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathbbm{1}(\|\widehat{T}_{i}\|^{2}-\|\widehat{U}_{i}\|^{2}\leq t)\xlongrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{}F_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}-\|U_{1}\|^{2}}(t). (246)

In particular, using the same arguments as for qn,αq_{n,\alpha}, we obtain that a.s.,

qn,α′′→n→∞Q‖T1‖2−‖U1‖2​(1−α)=q1−αℱ.\displaystyle q_{n,\alpha}^{\prime\prime}\xlongrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{}Q_{\|T_{1}\|^{2}-\|U_{1}\|^{2}}(1-\alpha)=q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathcal{F}}. (247)

We finish with proving equation (105). For this, observe that for all i∈{1,…,n},i\in\{1,\ldots,n\},

pi,n′′≤pi,n′≤pi,n′′+max1≤j≤n⁡n​(bXn)j2,\displaystyle p_{i,n}^{\prime\prime}\leq p_{i,n}^{\prime}\leq p_{i,n}^{\prime\prime}+\max_{1\leq j\leq n}n(b_{X}^{n})_{j}^{2}, (248)

hence

qn,α′′≤qn,α′≤qn,α′′+max1≤j≤n⁡n​(bXn)j2.\displaystyle q_{n,\alpha}^{\prime\prime}\leq q_{n,\alpha}^{\prime}\leq q_{n,\alpha}^{\prime\prime}+\max_{1\leq j\leq n}n(b_{X}^{n})_{j}^{2}. (249)

Using the same arguments as in the proof of Proposition 3.4, the assumption that 𝔼⁡[‖X1‖4​q]<+∞\mathbb{E}[\|X_{1}\|^{4q}]<+\infty for some q>1q>1 implies that

max1≤j≤n⁡n​(bXn)j2→n→∞ℙ0.\displaystyle\max_{1\leq j\leq n}n(b_{X}^{n})_{j}^{2}\xlongrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{\mathbb{P}}0. (250)

Combining equations (247) and (249), and using that a.s. convergence implies convergence in probability, we have that qn,α′→n→∞ℙq1−αℱq_{n,\alpha}^{\prime}\xlongrightarrow[n\rightarrow\infty]{\mathbb{P}}q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathcal{F}}, which finishes the proof. ∎
